Among the 41324 curves with surjective mod-3 image, End = Z and good reduction at 3, 19772 have bad reduction at 2; 360 of those are ordinary at 3 with ρ̄ unramified at 2, and 359 are 3-distinguished, hence modular by Theorem 9.5.5. In total Theorem A applies to 11384 + 359 = 11743 curves. The smallest conductor with bad reduction at 2 is 1982, for y² + (x + 1)y = −x⁵ + x⁴ − x³ + x².

nodes.title: Automorphy of odd potentially abelian GSp₄ representations (Lemma 10.2.5)
nodes.statement: Let ρ : G_Q → GSp₄(Q̄_p) be continuous, irreducible and de Rham at p. Suppose (1) ρ(G_L) is abelian for some finite Galois L/Q; (2) ν(ρ(c)) = −1 for complex conjugation c; (3) ρ is not finite up to twist (no character twist of ρ has finite image). Then ρ is automorphic: it is the Galois representation of an isobaric automorphic representation of GL₄(A_Q) obtained by automorphic induction and tensor products from Hecke characters and odd Artin representations.
hypotheses: Finite up to twist: some twist by a character has finite image.
Uses automorphic induction GL₂/E → GL₄/Q for quadratic E and the tensor product GL₂ × GL₂ → GL₄ (Ramakrishnan), requested from ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.5.
proofSteps: By ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.5 (potentially abelian nodes), ρ|_{G_L} ≅ ⊕_{i=1}^b χ_i^{⊕a} with ab = 4, ρ ≅ Ind_{G_{K_i}}^{G_Q} V_i, and b > 1 since ρ is not finite up to twist (Lemma 10.2.3).

b = 2: ρ ≅ Ind_{G_F}^{G_Q} V_i with F quadratic and V_i two-dimensional potentially abelian; by Lemma 10.2.4 (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison:ET.7a/induced-character-client) either both V_i are automorphic over F, so ρ is (automorphic induction), or both are finite up to twist. In the latter case ∧²ρ contains a character, so either det V_i extends to Q (then ρ is finite up to twist, excluded, by a square-root twist argument) or the Asai representation is reducible, giving V₁ ≅ V₂ ⊗ φ, so the projective representation of V_i extends to Q and lifts (Tate; G7/lifting-projective-representations): ρ ≅ V ⊗ Ind_{G_F}^{G_Q} χ with F imaginary quadratic, χ an algebraic Hecke character and V of finite image. If V is not induced, comparing the symplectic and orthogonal forms shows ν(c) = −1 forces V odd, so V is modular (odd Artin conjecture over Q, ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.1/odd-artin-modularity-over-q) and ρ is automorphic by the tensor product.
b = 4: ρ ≅ Ind_{G_K}^{G_Q} χ with K quartic containing an imaginary CM subfield (non-parallel weight); induce in two quadratic steps through E = K⁺ or an imaginary quadratic E ⊂ K.
acceptance: Remark 10.2.6: dropping oddness would include V ⊗ Ind χ with V even of projective image A₅; dropping (3) would include odd Artin representations with projective image S₆ ⊂ PGSp₄(C), whose modularity is unknown.

sources.match: Proves automorphy of an irreducible de Rham potentially abelian GSp₄-valued representation of G_Q with odd similitude that is not finite up to twist, by cases b = 2 and b = 4 in the decomposition of Lemma 10.2.3, using Lemma 10.2.4, the Asai decomposition of ∧², Tate's lifting theorem and the odd Artin conjecture.
Decompose a potentially abelian representation as an induction from character stabilizers and classify the two-dimensional case.
Explains which cases would remain without oddness or without the finite-up-to-twist hypothesis.

nodes.title: Automorphy for 32 of the 34 Galois types (Theorem 10.2.1)
nodes.statement: Let A/Q be an abelian surface whose Galois type in the sense of Fité–Kedlaya–Rotger–Sutherland (AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity:AP.6/galois-types) is neither A (End(A_{Q̄}) = Z) nor B[C₂] (End(A) = Z but End(A_K) ⊗ Q is Q × Q or a real quadratic field for some quadratic K/Q). Then A is modular in the sense of AM.0/isobaric-modularity. The excluded type B[C₂] contains Res_{K/Q}E for non-CM E/K not isogenous to its conjugate, and simple surfaces of GL₂-type over K such as the Jacobian of y² + (x³ + 1)y = x⁶ + 2x³ − x (LMFDB 12500.a.12500.1, K = Q(√5)).
hypotheses: A/Q an abelian surface; H¹(A) as in AM.0/isobaric-modularity; the classification of the representations ρ_{A,p} independent of p into (1) strongly irreducible (type A), (2) reducible, (3) potentially abelian but not reducible, (4) induced from a quadratic K/Q but not potentially abelian, subdivided into E[D_n] and B[C₂], is AP.6/galois-types (BCGP21 §9.2).
proofSteps: Reducible types: the compatible system splits as a sum of two irreducible odd regular rank-two systems; by Faltings (R28.4) A is then Q-isogenous to a product of elliptic curves or is of GL₂-type over Q, and is modular by EllipticCurveModularity:R29.6/modularity-theorem and EllipticCurveModularityPartIIGL2TypeAbelianVarieties:GT.3/modularity-theorem (Khare–Wintenberger for odd regular rank-two compatible systems, requested from ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.1).

Type E[D_n]: ρ_p ≅ s_p ⊗ Ind_{G_K}^{G_Q} ψ^{−1} for a quadratic K/Q, a finite-order ψ and an odd irreducible regular rank-two system s over Q, automorphic by Khare–Wintenberger; ρ is then automorphic by automorphic induction and the GL₂ × GL₂ tensor product (requested from ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.5).
Potentially abelian irreducible types: ρ_p has multiplier ε^{−1}, so ν(c) = −1, and distinct Hodge–Tate weights, so it is not finite up to twist; apply AM.8/potentially-abelian-automorphy.
acceptance: Remark 10.2.2: for real quadratic K, Res_{K/Q}E is modular via Freitas–Le Hung–Siksek; for imaginary quadratic K partial results are due to Caraiani–Newton.

Describes the surfaces of type B[C₂], restrictions of scalars of elliptic curves and simple GL₂-type surfaces over quadratic fields, with an LMFDB example over Q(√5).

nodes.title: The rational parameter space of genus-two curves with fixed 2-torsion (§10.3.5)
nodes.statement: Let F be a field of characteristic 0 (a number field or a local field) and ρ̄ : G_F → GSp₄(F₂) continuous. Through ι (AM.2/s6-sp4-identification), ρ̄ corresponds to a degree-6 étale F-algebra K = F[x]/f(x) (f separable of degree 6, the curve y² = f(x) having 2-torsion ρ̄). Fix the F-basis 1, x, …, x⁵ of K and identify K with the affine space A⁶_F. For θ ∈ K let χ_θ(T) be the characteristic polynomial of multiplication by θ, with roots σ_θ (the images of θ under the six geometric points of Spec K). Let Z(ρ̄) ⊂ A⁶_F be the complement of the hyperplanes σ_i(θ) = σ_j(θ), i ≠ j (defined over the splitting field; their union is defined over F). For θ ∈ Z(ρ̄)(F), X_θ : y² = χ_θ(x) is a smooth genus-two curve with Jac(X_θ)[2] ≅ ρ̄. Z(ρ̄) is a smooth rational variety, and the construction is compatible with field extensions and completions. For approximation use the enlarged family Z⁺(ρ̄) = Z(ρ̄) × G_m with X_{θ,c} : y² = c χ_θ(x). It is also smooth and rational and has the same 2-torsion, since a quadratic twist fixes the six branch points and acts trivially on 2-torsion. Every genus-two curve over an infinite characteristic-zero field with this marked six-point Galois set occurs in this family after a change of coordinate on its hyperelliptic quotient P¹: choose a rational nonbranch point for infinity, identify its finite branch algebra with K, and retain the nonzero leading coefficient c. The monic subfamily alone need not represent that local quadratic twist.
hypotheses: Characteristic 0; the hyperplanes are defined over the Galois closure of K and permuted by Galois.

The construction works with an affine chart of K from the start (the printed description in P⁶ needs a chart; PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-25/E072, rejected by the extraction's review, asked for this).
proofSteps: The six roots of χ_θ are the σ_i(θ), permuted by G_F as the points of Spec K(F̄), i.e. through ρ̄ under ι; when they are distinct the sextic is separable and X_θ is smooth of genus two with Weierstrass points the σ_i(θ), so Jac(X_θ)[2] ≅ ρ̄ (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A3/genus-two-two-torsion).
By the primitive element theorem, σ_i(θ) ≠ σ_j(θ) for θ outside finitely many hyperplanes; Z(ρ̄) is a non-empty open subset of A⁶, hence smooth and rational.
Base change of K along F → F′ (extensions or completions) gives Z(ρ̄|_{G_{F′}}) = Z(ρ̄) ×_F F′.

For the local-surjectivity assertion, the genus-two canonical map realizes the hyperelliptic quotient as P¹ over F. Move a rational nonbranch point to infinity, possible since F is infinite; the resulting sextic is c times a monic polynomial. Its branch algebra is the prescribed K via ι, so its coordinate is a primitive θ ∈ K with characteristic polynomial χ_θ. The multiplier c belongs to F×. Base change and smooth rationality persist under the product with G_m.
acceptance: Used with Lemma 9.4.1 in Lemma 10.3.6.

sources.match: Constructs, for a mod-2 representation, the degree-6 étale algebra and the open subset of its affine space of elements with distinct conjugates, whose rational points give genus-two curves y² = ∏(x − σ_θ) with prescribed 2-torsion, a smooth rational variety compatible with extensions and completions. The G_m enlargement and its local-seed property are the reviewer’s explicit adapter for the approximation use in Lemma 10.3.6, not an additional assertion attributed to §10.3.5.

nodes.title: Trivial Frobenius at 3 obstructs the local seed (Remark 10.3.8)
nodes.statement: If ρ̄ : G_Q → GSp₄(F₂) is unramified at 3 with ρ̄(Frob₃) = 1, there is no genus-two curve X with good reduction at 3 and Jac(X)[2] ≅ ρ̄ as G_{Q₃}-modules, and no product E₁ × E₂ of elliptic curves with good ordinary reduction at 3 and trivial 2-torsion action of Frob₃.
hypotheses: ρ̄ unramified at 3 with trivial Frobenius.
proofSteps: Trivial Frob₃ makes the six Weierstrass points of X rational over Q₃; with good reduction at 3 they reduce to six distinct ramification points of the degree-2 map to P¹ over F₃, but P¹(F₃) has 4 points.
For E/F₃ with #E[2](F₃) = 4, the Hasse bound (Tau Ceti EllipticCurves layer 3) gives #E(F₃) = 4, so a₃ = 0 and E is supersingular.
acceptance: This is why Lemma 10.3.6 and Theorem 10.3.9 assume ρ̄(Frob₃) ≠ 1.

sources.match: Explains that the method of Lemma 10.3.6 fails for trivial Frobenius at 3, since six rational Weierstrass points cannot reduce to distinct points of P¹(F₃), and products of elliptic curves with full rational 2-torsion over F₃ are supersingular by the Hasse bound.

nodes.title: Realizing an ordinary mod-2 representation by a good surface (Lemma 10.3.6, corrected)
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄ : G_Q → GSp₄(F₂) be continuous, unramified at 3 with ρ̄(Frob₃) ≠ 1, and suppose ρ̄ has a finite flat model W/Z₂ that is ordinary (an extension of an étale group scheme by a multiplicative one) and isomorphic to its Cartier dual. Then there is an abelian surface A/Q with (1) good ordinary reduction at 3 and 3-distinguished; (2) good ordinary reduction at 2, A[2]/Z₂ ≅ W, and Frobenius polynomial Q(x) at 2 with Q(x) ≢ (x² ± x + 2)² mod 3; (3) ρ̄_{A,3} surjective; (4) ρ̄_{A,2} ≅ ρ̄. The local input at 3 for the partition [2,2,2] is the Weil restriction Res_{F₉/F₃}E of E : y² = x(x − 1)(x − t), t² = −1, lifted to a nearby Jacobian over Q₃ with good ordinary Jacobian reduction and the same mod-2 representation (correction of the printed curve, which is not 3-distinguished); the local input at 2 is the ordinary dyadic finite-level lifting of AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A4/ordinary-dyadic-finite-level-lifting, whose scope as corrected (skew self-duality versus alternation) is the polarization obligation recorded as a gap.
hypotheses: W is part of the hypothesis: ρ̄ does not determine W (two non-isomorphic W with conjugate generic fibres are given in the proof).
Corrections: PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-25/E053 (the [2,2,2] seed), E050 and E051 (the integral H² and alternation steps of Lemma 10.3.1), E071 (H¹_f(Q₂, μ₂)).
The integral polarized lifting and local-neighbourhood contracts below remain proof obligations: this node records a conditional target, not a proved realization from Cartier self-duality alone.
proofSteps: Work on Z⁺ = Z(ρ̄) × G_m (AM.8/mod-two-parameter-space), smooth and rational; the conditions at 2 and 3 are open in Z⁺(Q₂), Z⁺(Q₃) (Kisin's local constancy, requested from NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties:R11.6), surjectivity of ρ̄_{A,3} holds outside a thin set using the A4 generic-monodromy request and IG.2, so AM.6/thin-set-approximation reduces everything to finding local points. Each local curve is represented by a point (θ,c), so no assumption that its leading coefficient is a square is needed.

At 3: ρ̄ unramified, so K ⊗ Q₃ is given by one of the ten non-trivial partitions of 6; nine are realized by explicit curves over Q (Table on p. 220, conductors 1051, 709, 1415, 389, 847, 349, 353, 4889, 1343) with good ordinary 3-distinguished reduction. For [2,2,2] the printed curve (conductor 7165) has Q₃ = (x² + 2x + 3)², not 3-distinguished; use Res_{F₉/F₃}E (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6/finite-etale-weil-restriction-of-abelian-schemes) and the lift/Torelli/local-constancy bridge (A4/genus-two-jacobian-lifting and the gap PO-local-three).

At 2: W is an extension of an étale V by its Cartier dual, and V is trivial, of order 2 non-semisimple, or semisimple of order 3; the curves of the table on p. 221 (conductors 3451, 2225, 713, partitions [1⁶], [2,2,2], [3,3]) give ordinary A₀/F₂ of each type (for [2,2,2] the model y² + (x³ + 1)y = −3x⁴ + 4x² + 2x with Jac(C)(F₂) ≅ Z/14 shows V is not trivial). Condition (10.3.7) on Q(x) mod 3 holds for the chosen A₀ by AM.4/weil-quartics-at-two.

nodes.title: Ordinary residual modularity modulo 2 (Theorem 10.3.9)
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄ : G_Q → GSp₄(F₂) be continuous, unramified at 3 with ρ̄(Frob₃) ≠ 1, with an ordinary finite flat model W/Z₂ isomorphic to its Cartier dual. Then ρ̄ is ordinarily modular of weight 2 and level prime to 6: there is a cuspidal π of GSp₄(A_Q) of weight 2 with central character |·|², spherical at 2 and 3 and ordinary at 2, with ρ̄_{π,2} ≅ ρ̄. In particular this holds for mod-2 representations with image A₆ or S₆ satisfying the local hypotheses.
hypotheses: The hypotheses of AM.8/mod-two-realization; conditional on its recorded local obligations and on the inputs of AM.7/fifteen-image-modularity.
proofSteps: Take A from AM.8/mod-two-realization. Condition (10.3.7) excludes 4C and 12C at 2 (AM.1/frobenius-class-at-two); A has good ordinary 3-distinguished reduction at 3 and surjective ρ̄_{A,3}, so AM.7/fifteen-image-modularity (via AM.7/theorem-a) makes A modular through a weight-2 π.

Use the AP.0 pure local comparison and spherical ordinary packet-choice adapter at 2 and 3 for the surface A with good reduction there. Choose the weight-2 cuspidal member spherical at both primes and ordinary at 2; its ordinary-at-2 attachment gives ρ̄_{π,2} ≅ ρ̄_{A,2} ≅ ρ̄. These local choices and attachments are a supplier contract, not a formal consequence of an attachment initially made only at 3.
acceptance: The residual images A₆ and S₆ are the cases advertised in §1.5 and §10.

sources.match: Deduces that a mod-2 representation unramified at 3 with non-trivial Frobenius there and an ordinary Cartier self-dual finite flat model at 2 is ordinarily modular of weight 2 and level prime to 6, by applying Theorem 9.5.2 to the surface of Lemma 10.3.6.
